decisions.note: Measured on a 600 dpi strip of p.074. In the 1st dua the gap between the period and «[» is 18 px. That is the same as the ')' to '.' gap (19 px), so only the glyph side bearings separate them and no space is printed: «(ثلاثًا).[تقرأ». In the 2nd dua the same gap is 40 px, an extra word space: «(ثلاثًا). [تقرأ». Kept tight as printed, following the b17/b18 precedent of copying tight spacing.

At 450 dpi «مُحَمَّدٍ» looks heavier than «وَبسيدنا» and «نَبِيًّا». This is the body font's special محمد ligature, and it looks the same in «سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِكَ» on p.049 (zoomed for comparison). That p.049 instance is unmarked in final b13, as are all other مُحَمَّدٍ in finals b13/b17/b21/b27. It is not contrasting bold emphasis, so no ** is used.

At 800 dpi a kasra is printed low under the Allah ligature in «بِكَلِمَاتِ الله التَّامَّاتِ». It sits separately from the kasra under the ت of كلمات and from the letters of التامات. A case vowel is printed, so the Name is written with all its marks per CONVENTIONS §2: اللَّهِ. This follows the b18 d003 precedent for بِاللَّهِ.

print_errors.note: The phrase is fully vowelled, but the final mim of «وَعَظِيم» has no kasra. I checked this at 1400 dpi: there is a kasra under the za and nothing under the mim. Kept as printed, with no kasra added.
The first waw has no fatha (checked at 2000 dpi). Every other conjunction waw in this dua has one (وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ، وَبسيدنا). Kept as printed.

keyA.notes: Markers: p.072 ends with a complete sentence («[البقرة: ٢٨٤-٢٨٦].») and has no footnotes. p.073 starts with a new basmala + al-Kafirun, so it is <<<ص:073>>>. p.073 ends inside al-Nas, after «ٱلْخَنَّاسِ». p.074 continues the surah and opens with the ayah-4 end ornament «(٤)», so it is <<<ص:074+>>>. Because validate.py needs ﴿﴾ balanced on each line, the al-Nas quotation is closed with ﴾ at the end of p.073 and reopened with ﴿ at the start of p.074; neither bracket is printed at the page break (same handling as b18 p.071/072). The ayah-end number (٤), printed at the top of p.074, is kept there: «﴿(٤) ٱلَّذِى…». p.075 and p.076 each start with a new parenthesised dua, so they have no '+'. p.076 ends mid-dua with «…إِلَّا أَنْتَ،» and the parenthesis open; it continues on p.077. No footnotes, headings or poetry on these pages. Quran: scripts/quran.py reports no flags for the whole batch. Encoding follows CONVENTIONS §3 / Tanzil: rectangular zero on أَنَا۠ (109:4; an upright oval, checked at 1000 dpi); round silent zero on فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ (106:3; checked at 2600 dpi); iqlab high mim on تَوَّابًۢا and أَحَدٌۢ; low mim under the kasratan of خَوْفٍۭ; small yeh in إِۦلَٰفِهِمْ; madda on ٱلَّذِىٓ (106:4); small waw on إِنَّهُۥ، لَّهُۥ، يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ, but not on «لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ» (not printed there). Waqf signs are written where printed: ۚ after وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ (110:3); 59:22-24 ۖ ۖ ۚ ۖ ۚ ۖ. Each surah basmala is printed before the bracket and written outside it. References: Arabic-Indic digits in logical order (١-٦ etc.). Spacing was measured at 1000 dpi. The colon-to-digit gap is about 76-85 px, so a space is written after every colon ([الكافرون: ١-٦], [الحشر: ٢٢-٢٤] …). The gap between «]» and «(ثلاثًا)» on p.073/074 is about 55 px (twice the bracket side bearing), so a space is written: «[الإخلاص: ١-٤] (ثلاثًا).» This differs from b17 p.068, where the gap was about 27 px and no space was written. A space is always written between ﴾ and [. «(ثلاثًا)» has fathatan only, except «(ثَلاثًا)» with fatha on the first tha after al-Falaq (p.073) and on p.075 (2nd dua); each instance was checked. Reading notes «[تقرأ مرة واحدة للمتعجل]»: on p.074, 1st dua, the period and «[» are set tight («).[تقرأ», gap about 16 px against about 65 px elsewhere), so no space is written there; all the others have «). [تقرأ». Lam-alif: in this body font the left diagonal stroke is the alif and the right upright is the lam. This was checked against the hamza position in الأَرْضِ / الْأَذَى and the madda in الْآخِرَةِ, all at 2400 dpi. The fatha is over the alif stroke in «لاَ إِلَهَ» (p.074, last dua), «لاَ يَضُرُّ» and «وَلاَ فِي» (p.075), and those are written لاَ. Everywhere else it is over the lam stroke: لَا, and إِلَّا with shadda+fatha on the lam. «الأَرْضِ» (p.075) has hamza+fatha on the alif and a sukun on the ra, but no sukun on the lam (2400 dpi); «وَالْآخِرَةِ» (p.075), «وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ» (p.075) and «الْأَذَى» (p.076) do have the sukun on the lam. Allah: plain الله wherever only the ligature's own shadda/small alif are drawn (بِالله ×2, سُبْحَانَ الله ×3, بِسْمِ الله). On p.075 «بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ» has a kasra printed low under the ha of the Allah ligature (2200 dpi), so it is written اللَّهِ, as in b18 p.071. «اللَّهُمَّ» is always explicitly vowelled. Final ى drawn with the Lotus automatic small alif is written plain: عَلَى (p.074, p.076 ×2), أَمْسَى (p.075), الْأَذَى (p.076). In Quran, ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ keeps its dagger alif. Bold: on p.075 «مُحَمَّدٍ» is set in a clearly heavier face than «وَبسيدنا» and «نَبِيًّا» around it, so it is **مُحَمَّدٍ**, followed by the ﷺ glyph. «وَبسيدنا» has only the fatha on the waw. The «(ثلاثًا)» and «[تقرأ…]» notes and the duas are in the regular face, so no bold. Other details checked at high zoom: «مِن نِّعْمَةٍ» (p.075) has no sukun on the nun of مِن and shadda+kasra on the nun of نِّعْمَةٍ, as printed. The fatha on the final kaf (بِكَ، لَكَ، نِعْمَتَكَ، بِنِعْمَتِكَ، سُبْحَانَكَ …) is printed high on the kaf's ascender and was confirmed on each. «[أَمْسَيْتُ]» / «[أَمْسَى]» keep their square brackets. Running heads, page numbers, bracket flowers and ayah ornaments are omitted, except for the digits inside them.

print_errors.note: The final م of وَعَظِيم has no kasra. Checked at 1100 dpi. Every other word in this dua is fully vowelled, so وَعَظِيمِ was probably intended. Kept as printed.
The conjunction و has no fatha, while every other و in these duas carries one (checked at 1100 dpi). Kept as printed.

keyB.notes: Markers: p072 ends with a complete «[البقرة: ٢٨٤-٢٨٦].» and has no footnotes, so p073 has no + and no (تابع). Surat an-Nas runs over the p073/p074 page turn: the line breaks after «ٱلْخَنَّاسِ» and p074 starts with the ayah-4 ornament (٤). So p074 is marked +. As in keyB b17/b18, ﴾ was added at the end of p073 and ﴿ at the start of p074 so that each line is balanced for validate.py. A merge should remove these two brackets. The ayah number (٤) stays where it is printed, at the top of p074. p075 and p076 each begin a new paragraph after «(ثلاثًا).», so they have no +. p076 ends mid-sentence («…إِلَّا أَنْتَ،»); p077 continues it. There are no footnotes, headings, glosses or bold markup on pp.073-076. Quran: every span was read from 500-1400 dpi zooms. scripts/quran.py reports no difference from Tanzil. Encodings: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا (dagger alif + madda, no tatweel); أَنَا۠ (upright oval zero U+06E0, checked at 1000 dpi); فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ (round zero U+06DF, checked at 1400 dpi); iqlab tanween تَوَّابًۢا and أَحَدٌۢ (single haraka + small high meem printed, encoded as tanween + U+06E2 as in keyB b12/b16/b17); خَوْفٍۭ (kasra + small low meem, U+06ED); إِۦلَٰفِهِمْ (the small mark after إِ is the KFGQPC small yeh, U+06E6); dotless final ى as printed in فِى، وَلِىَ، ٱلَّذِى، ٱلَّذِىٓ. Waqf signs ۚ (110:3, 59:23, 59:24) and ۖ (59:22 twice, 59:24 twice) are printed and transcribed. The small calligraphic basmala before each surah or passage is written as the standard basmala outside the brackets. References use Arabic-Indic digits on these pages, including [الناس: ١-٦] on p074 (p069 used European digits). Ranges are written in logical order. A space after the colon is printed in every reference. The visible gap before the colon in «[النصر:» and «[الحشر:» comes from the shape of the ر tail, so no space was written there. The print sets «﴾[الحشر» touching; it is written with one space, as in earlier keyB batches. «(ثلاثًا)» carries a fatha on ث only after al-Falaq (p073) and in the second dua of p075 («(ثَلاثًا)»); all other occurrences have no fatha. These were checked one by one at 700-900 dpi. Lam-alif marks were checked as ASCII ink maps at 800 dpi. The upright stroke is the lam and the slanted stroke is the alif, as in keyB b13. Fatha on the lam: لَا on p074 (lines 4, 9, 11 and 15), p075 (لَا شَرِيكَ) and p076 (لَا يَمُوتُ، لَا إِلَهَ). Fatha on the alif: «لاَ إِلَهَ» (p074, dua «أَنْتَ رَبِّي»), «لاَ يَضُرُّ» and «وَلاَ فِي» (p075). Shadda+fatha in every إِلَّا is on the lam. Fathatan in ورَسُولًا is on the lam. In لِجَلَالِ and وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ the fatha is on the lam. In الْآخِرَةِ، الْإِسْلَامِ and الْأَذَى the sukun sits over the lam. الأَرْضِ (p075) has no sukun on the lam, as printed. «كَمَا» (p075 and twice on p076) has two separate fathas, one on ك and one on م, confirmed by ink maps. The word Allah is written with only its printed case vowel, as in earlier keyB batches. On p075 «بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ» has a printed kasra that sits low, below the line under the ه of the ligature (checked by ink map), so it is written اللهِ. The other occurrences (بِالله ×2، سُبْحَانَ الله ×3، بِسْمِ الله) show no case mark even in zooms that include the space below the line. Final ى with the body font's automatic small alif is written plain (عَلَى، [أَمْسَى]، الْأَذَى). مُحَمَّدٍ on p075 looks heavier than its neighbours. This is the font's محمد ligature, which looks the same on p049 where keyB did not mark it, so no ** was used. The ﷺ glyph is kept as U+FDFA. Spacing: p074 prints «(ثلاثًا).[تقرأ» with no space after the period (first dua). Like the other six instances, it is written «(ثلاثًا). [تقرأ», following the keyB one-space normalisation (b14, b16). «واحدة للمتعجل» is set tight in some lines but is written as two words. Paragraphs follow the printed indents. p076 «[تَحَصَّنْتُ … (اصْرِفْ … قَدِيرٌ) (ثلاثًا)] (ثلاثًا).» keeps the printed nesting of brackets. Zoom images: scratch\b19_*.png, scratch\b19t_*.png.
